about: The harness's steps, written once. The process page (process_page.py) and the process figures (figures.py) are both drawn from this file. who: us (the researchers), model, or program (ordinary code that gives the same output for the same input). check: a point where we decide. status: built, or being rebuilt for codebook version 1.0.

us.name: Us
us.why: Research decisions: what to ask, what to read, what enters the codebook, what the findings mean.

model.name: Model
model.why: Reading for meaning at a scale people cannot. Every output is checked by the program and decided by us.

program.name: Program
program.why: Work that must come out the same every time: splitting, numbering, copying, checking, counting, applying rules. Free, instant, and anyone can rerun it.

phases.name: Build the codebook
phases.containers: The groups from Stage 1 are the containers. At the start they are empty; the papers fill them.
phases.out: Codebook version 1.0 and the codebook trail

steps.what: Write the question, sub-questions and groups (the containers)
Choose the papers, with a reason for each
Split each paper into numbered passages
Read each paper whole; put each idea in a container, citing its passages
Check every cited passage exists; copy the quoted words
Merge ideas that say the same thing, within each container
steps.record: Drafted codes; ideas set aside, with reasons

steps.what: Check that no idea went missing
Decide each code: level 1, level 2, reference or reject, with reasons
Search the whole paper for links no cited sentence confirms
Judge each shortlisted link
Confirm the judged links
Freeze the codebook, with fingerprints of every input

phases.name: Code the interviews
phases.containers: The same groups, now holding the frozen codes. Each tick names its story; what fits no code goes to the anomaly code.
phases.out: A coded round, and the next version of the codebook

steps.what: Draw the round's 25 interviews by a recorded seed
Split each interview into numbered segments
Code the whole interview: reason, then tick each code under its story, citing segments
steps.record: The model's coding file, every reason, and what the checks removed

steps.what: Code the same interviews on the coding page
Check codes and segments; work out level 2 by rule
steps.record: Definitions, rivals and types per story

steps.what: Compare coders; count agreement and anomalies
steps.record: Agreement report, near misses, code use (comparison/)
steps.status: built; tested on made-up researcher coding

steps.what: Review the round; group anomalies into themes
Read papers for adopted themes; write next codebook
steps.record: Searches and papers kept in the anomaly log; codebook_v<next>.json; progression page
